title.zh: 卷一百五十六 列傳第八十一 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢
title.en: Volume 156 Biographies 81: Yang, Dai, Yang, two Li's, Han, Du, Xing
title.raw: 卷一百五十六 列傳第八十一 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢 Volume 156 Biographies 81: Yang, Dai, Yang, two Li's, Han, Du, Xing

sentences.zh: 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢

translations.literal: Yang, Dai, Yang, two Li's, Han, Du, Xing
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Dai, Yang, the two Lis, Han, Du, and Xing

sentences.zh: 楊朝晟

translations.literal: Yang Zhaosheng
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhaosheng

sentences.zh: 楊朝晟，字叔明，夏州朔方人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhaosheng, styled Shuming, was a man of Shuofang in Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhaosheng, courtesy name Shuming, came from Shuofang in Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 興行間，以先鋒功授甘泉府果毅。

translations.literal: During the Xingyuan era, for merit as vanguard he was appointed fruiti-corps commander of Ganquan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xingyuan period he earned appointment as fruiti-corps commander of Ganquan Prefecture for distinguished service in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，從李懷光討劉文喜涇州，斬獲多，加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, he followed Li Huaiguang to campaign against Liu Wenxi at Jing Prefecture; kills and captures were many, and he was promoted to General of the Indomitable Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign he followed Li Huaiguang against Liu Wenxi at Jing Prefecture, took many heads and captives, and was promoted to General of the Indomitable Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李納寇徐州，從唐朝臣往討，常冠軍。

translations.literal: When Li Na raided Xuzhou, he followed Tang Chaochen to attack and often led the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na invaded Xuzhou, he marched with Tang Chaochen to suppress him and repeatedly led the van.

sentences.zh: 懷光赴難奉天，屬朝晟兵千人下咸陽，賜實封百五十戶。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang went to relieve the crisis at Fengtian, he placed a thousand of Zhaosheng's troops under him to descend on Xianyang, and Zhaosheng was granted a substantive fief of one hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiguang rushed to the emperor's aid at Fengtian, he assigned Zhaosheng a thousand men to advance on Xianyang, and the court granted him a substantive fief of one hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 懷光反，韓遊瑰退保邠、寧，賊黨張昕守邠州，大索軍實，多募士，欲潛歸之。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang rebelled, Han Yougui withdrew to hold Bin and Ning; the rebel partisan Zhang Xin held Bin Prefecture, searched broadly for military stores, recruited many men, and wished secretly to go over to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiguang turned rebel, Han Yougui fell back to defend Bin and Ning; the rebel agent Zhang Xin held Bin Prefecture, requisitioned military supplies on a wide scale, enlisted many troops, and planned to defect to Huaiguang in secret.

sentences.zh: 朝晟父懷賓為遊瑰將，夜以數十騎斬昕及同謀者。

translations.literal: Zhaosheng's father Huaibin was a general under Yougui; by night with several dozen horsemen he beheaded Xin and his fellow conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosheng's father Huaibin served under Yougui; one night he rode out with several dozen men and killed Xin and his co-conspirators.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰遣懷賓告行在，德宗勞問，授兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Yougui sent Huaibin to report to the imperial camp; Emperor Dezong commended and questioned him and appointed him acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui sent Huaibin to announce the deed to the emperor's camp; Dezong received him with praise and inquiry and appointed him acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 朝晟泣見懷光曰：「父立功於國，子當誅，不可以主兵。

translations.literal: Zhaosheng wept as he went to see Huaiguang and said, "My father has rendered merit to the state; his son ought to be put to death and must not command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosheng went to Huaiguang in tears and said, "My father has won glory for the realm; I, his son, deserve execution and must not be allowed to lead soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」懷光縶之。

translations.literal: " Huaiguang had him bound.
translations.idiomatic: " Huaiguang had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 及諸軍圍河中，遊瑰營長春宮，而懷賓戰甚力。

translations.literal: When the various armies besieged Hezhong, Yougui encamped at Changchun Palace, and Huaibin fought with great force.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies besieged Hezhong, Yougui encamped at Changchun Palace while Huaibin fought with exceptional vigor.

sentences.zh: 懷光平，帝原朝晟，因為遊瑰都虞候。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang was pacified, the emperor pardoned Zhaosheng and made him Yougui's chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiguang's defeat the emperor pardoned Zhaosheng and appointed him chief adjutant under Yougui.

sentences.zh: 父子皆開府、賓客、御史中丞，軍中以為榮。

translations.literal: Father and son both held grand preceptorate appointments, were retainers, and served as Vice Censors-in-Chief; within the army this was regarded as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son alike held grand preceptorate titles, served as household guests, and bore the rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief—a distinction the army took as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃犯邊，遊瑰自將守寧州，而禦士寬，軍驕。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided the frontier, Yougui personally led troops to guard Ning Prefecture, but in controlling the men he was lenient and the army grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans struck the border, Yougui took command in person to hold Ning Prefecture; his discipline was lax, and the troops grew insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 及張獻甫來代，軍遂亂，朝晟逃於郊。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xianfu came to replace him, the army thereupon mutinied, and Zhaosheng fled to the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xianfu arrived to replace him, the army mutinied at once, and Zhaosheng escaped into the outskirts.

sentences.zh: 眾脅監軍，請以范希朝為節度使。

translations.literal: The masses coerced the army supervisor and requested that Fan Xichao be made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers seized the army supervisor and demanded that Fan Xichao be made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 希朝時已在京師。

translations.literal: Xichao was then already in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao was already in the capital at the time.

sentences.zh: 明日，朝晟出，紿眾曰：「予來賀所請之當也。

translations.literal: The next day Zhaosheng came forth and deceived the crowd, saying, "I have come to congratulate you on the appropriateness of your request.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhaosheng appeared and told the troops, "I have come to congratulate you on asking for the right man.

sentences.zh: 」眾稍定。

translations.literal: " The crowd gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The men calmed somewhat.

sentences.zh: 朝晟結諸將謀誅首惡者。

translations.literal: Zhaosheng joined the generals in plotting to execute the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosheng rallied the commanders to plot the execution of the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 居三日，紿遣人自邠來，曰：「前請報罷，張公已舍邠矣，反者皆當死，吾不願盡誅也，第取首惡者。

translations.literal: After three days he deceptively sent a man from Bin, who said, "The earlier request has been denied; Lord Zhang has already left Bin. Rebels all ought to die, but I do not wish to execute them all—only take the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he sent a messenger from Bin with a fabricated report: "Your petition has been refused; Lord Zhang has already quit Bin. Every rebel deserves death, but I do not mean to slaughter you all—only the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 」眾所讙指，斬二百餘人，獻甫遂入於軍。

translations.literal: " Those whom the crowd cheered and pointed out were beheaded—more than two hundred men—and Xianfu thereupon entered the army.
translations.idiomatic: " The men the crowd denounced were beheaded—more than two hundred—and Xianfu was able to take command.

sentences.zh: 帝以希朝為節度副使，而朝晟加御史大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor made Xichao deputy military commissioner, while Zhaosheng was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Xichao deputy commissioner and promoted Zhaosheng to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年，城鹽州，發卒護境，朝晟屯木波堡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan, Salt Prefecture was fortified and troops were dispatched to guard the border; Zhaosheng encamped at Mubo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan the court fortified Salt Prefecture and sent troops to guard the frontier; Zhaosheng garrisoned Mubo Fort.

sentences.zh: 會獻甫卒，有詔代為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: When Xianfu died, an edict appointed him to replace him as military commissioner of Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfu died, an edict named Zhaosheng military commissioner of Bin-Ning in his place.

sentences.zh: 朝晟請城方渠，合道，木波以遏吐蕃路。

translations.literal: Zhaosheng requested to fortify Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo to block the Tibetan route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosheng proposed building fortresses at Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo to choke off Tibetan advances.

sentences.zh: 詔問：「須兵幾何？

translations.literal: An edict asked, "How many troops are needed?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked by edict, "How many troops will you need?

sentences.zh: 」報曰：「部兵可辦。

translations.literal: " He reported, "The troops of the command can manage it.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The forces of my command can handle it.

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「前日城五原，興師七萬，今何易邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked, "The other day in fortifying Wuyuan we raised an army of seventy thousand—why is it so easy now?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "When we fortified Wuyuan we mobilized seventy thousand men—why is this so easy now?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「鹽州之役，虜先知之。

translations.literal: " He answered, "In the Salt Prefecture campaign the enemy knew beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "At Salt Prefecture the barbarians learned of our plans in advance.

sentences.zh: 今薄戎而城，虜料王師不十萬，勢難輕入。

translations.literal: Now, pressing close to the barbarians while building fortresses, the enemy will reckon the imperial army at fewer than one hundred thousand and will find it hard to enter lightly.
translations.idiomatic: This time we will build close to their territory; they will assume the imperial host is under one hundred thousand and will not dare strike lightly.

sentences.zh: 若發部兵，十日至塞下，未三旬城畢，積芻聚糧，留卒守之，寇至不可拔，萊野翦夷，虜且走，此萬全計也。

translations.literal: If we dispatch the command's troops, in ten days they reach the border; before thirty days the fortresses are complete, fodder and grain are amassed, and garrisons are left to hold them—when the enemy comes they cannot be taken, the fields and wilds are cleared, the barbarians will withdraw, and this is a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: Send only my command's troops: in ten days they reach the frontier, in less than thirty the walls are finished, fodder and grain stockpiled, and a garrison left behind. When raiders come they cannot take the forts; we clear the countryside, the enemy retreats, and the plan is foolproof.

sentences.zh: 若大發兵，閱月乃至，虜亦來，來必戰，戰則不暇城矣。

translations.literal: If a great army is raised, after a month it arrives and the barbarians also come; when they come there must be battle, and with battle there is no leisure to build fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilize a huge army and a month passes before it arrives; the enemy comes too, battle is inevitable, and there will be no time to build.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其策。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his plan.

sentences.zh: 師次方渠，水乏。

translations.literal: The army halted at Fangqu; water was scarce.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Fangqu, where water was scarce.

sentences.zh: 有青蛇降險下走，視其跡，水從而流，朝晟使築防環之，遂為渟淵，士飲仰足，圖其事以聞。

translations.literal: A green serpent descended the cliff and went downward; following its tracks, water flowed after it. Zhaosheng had a dike built to encircle it, and it became a still pool; the soldiers drank their fill, and he diagrammed the affair and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: A green serpent was seen slithering down the cliff; where it passed, water followed. Zhaosheng had a retaining wall built around the spring, forming a deep pool from which the men drank their fill; he recorded the event and reported it to court.

sentences.zh: 有詔置祠，命泉曰應聖。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a shrine established and named the spring Responsive to the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a shrine erected and named the spring "Responsive to the Sage."

sentences.zh: 已城，吐蕃悉眾至，度不能害，乃引去。

translations.literal: After the fortresses were completed, the Tibetans came with their full strength, judged that they could do no harm, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the fortifications were finished the Tibetans marched in full force, saw they could do no harm, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復城馬嶺而歸，開地三百里。

translations.literal: He again fortified Maling and returned, opening three hundred li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Maling as well and returned, opening three hundred li of new territory.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於屯。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died at his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 戴休顏 弟戴休璿 戴休晏

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan; younger brothers Dai Xiuxuan and Dai Xiuyan
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan; his younger brothers Dai Xiuxuan and Dai Xiuyan

sentences.zh: 戴休顏，字休顏，夏州人。

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan, styled Xiuyan, was a man of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan, courtesy name Xiuyan, was a native of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家世尚武，誌膽不常。

translations.literal: His family for generations esteemed martial affairs; his ambition and courage were extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long honored the martial arts, and his resolve and daring were out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀引為大將，諭平党項羌，以安河曲。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi brought him in as a great general and instructed him to pacify the Tangut and Qiang so as to secure the bend of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi took him on as a senior commander and charged him with pacifying the Tangut and Qiang to secure the Yellow River bend.

sentences.zh: 試太常卿，封濟陰郡公，進封咸寧郡王，兼朔方節度副使。

translations.literal: He was tried as Minister of Ceremonies, enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyin Commandery, advanced to Prince of Xianning Commandery, and concurrently made deputy military commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He served provisionally as Minister of Ceremonies, was enfeoffed Duke of Jiyin, advanced to Prince of Xianning, and named deputy commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 城邠州功最，遷鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: In fortifying Bin Prefecture his merit was greatest, and he was transferred to be prefect of Salt Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His contribution to the fortification of Bin Prefecture ranked first, and he was transferred to prefect of Salt Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，率兵三千晝夜馳，奔問行在，德宗嘉之，賜實戶二百。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he led three thousand troops in day-and-night gallop to rush to the imperial camp; Emperor Dezong commended him and granted two hundred substantive households.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled he raced day and night with three thousand men to the emperor's camp; Dezong praised him and granted two hundred substantive households.

sentences.zh: 與渾瑊、杜希全、韓遊瑰等扞禦有勞。

translations.literal: Together with Hun Jian, Du Xiquan, Han Yougui, and others he had merit in defense and resistance.
translations.idiomatic: With Hun Jian, Du Xiquan, Han Yougui, and others he earned distinction in the defense of the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝進狩梁、洋，留守奉天。

translations.literal: When the emperor advanced to hunt in Liang and Yang, he remained to guard Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew toward Liang and Yang, he stayed behind to hold Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 李懷光屯咸陽，使人誘之，休顏斬其使，勒兵自守。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang encamped at Xianyang and sent men to entice him; Xiuyan beheaded the envoy and urged the troops to hold themselves on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang camped at Xianyang and sent envoys to win him over; Xiuyan executed the messenger and rallied his men to stand firm.

sentences.zh: 懷光眙駭，自涇陽夜走。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was startled and wide-eyed and fled by night from Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was stunned and fled Jingyang under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校工部尚書、奉天行營節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Fengtian field army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Minister of Works and commissioner of the Fengtian field command.

sentences.zh: 合渾瑊兵破泚偏師，斬首三千級，追至中渭橋。

translations.literal: Joining Hun Jian's troops he defeated Ci's detached force, beheaded three thousand, and pursued to the Middle Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Hun Jian he routed Zhu Ci's flank force, took three thousand heads, and pursued to the Middle Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 京師平，又與瑊率兵趨岐陽，邀泚殘黨。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he again led troops with Jian to hurry to Qiyang and intercept Ci's remnant partisans.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered he marched again with Jian toward Qiyang to cut off Zhu Ci's remnants.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書右僕射，進戶四百。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and advanced four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted four hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 從乘輿至京師，賜女樂、甲第，拜左龍武軍統軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage to the capital, was granted female musicians and a mansion, and appointed commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted the emperor back to the capital, received female musicians and a grand residence, and was named commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弟休璿，歷開府儀同三司，封東陽郡王；

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiuxuan successively held Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiuxuan rose to Grand Preceptor with equipage equal to the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang;

sentences.zh: 休晏，歷輔國大將軍，封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: Xiuyan successively held General Who Assists the State and was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyan served as General Who Assists the State and was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 俱以將略稱。

translations.literal: Both were famed for military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Both were renowned for generalship.

sentences.zh: 陽惠元

translations.literal: Yang Huiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huiyuan

sentences.zh: 陽惠元，平州人。

translations.literal: Yang Huiyuan was a man of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huiyuan was a native of Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以趫勇奮，事平盧軍。

translations.literal: For leaping courage and ardor he served in the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for swift daring, he served in the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 從田神功、李忠臣浮海入青州。

translations.literal: He followed Tian Shenggong and Li Zhongchen across the sea into Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Tian Shenggong and Li Zhongchen by sea into Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔以兵隸神策，為京西兵馬使，鎮奉天。

translations.literal: An edict placed his troops under the Shence Army; he became military commissioner of troops west of the capital and garrisoned Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: By edict his troops were attached to the Shence Army; he became commissioner of capital-west forces and garrisoned Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 德宗初立，稍繩諸節度跋扈者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong first took the throne, he gradually reined in the overbearing military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Dezong's accession he began reining in overbearing regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 於是李正己屯曹州，田悅增河上兵，河南大擾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Zhengji encamped at Cao Prefecture, Tian Yue increased troops on the river, and Henan was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji then massed troops at Cao Prefecture, Tian Yue reinforced his forces on the Yellow River, and Henan fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 詔移兵萬二千戍關東，帝御望春樓誓師，因勞遣諸將。

translations.literal: An edict shifted twelve thousand troops to garrison the east of the pass; the emperor attended at Wangchun Tower to swear in the army and thereupon comforted and dispatched the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve thousand troops were ordered east of the pass; the emperor reviewed them at Wangchun Tower, administered the oath of campaign, and sent the commanders off with words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 酒至神策，將士不敢飲。

translations.literal: When wine reached the Shence troops, officers and soldiers did not dare to drink.
translations.idiomatic: When the toast reached the Shence contingent, the men refused to drink.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，惠元曰：「初發奉天，臣之帥張巨濟與眾約：『是役也，不立功，毋飲酒！

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; Huiyuan said, "When we first set out from Fengtian, my commander Zhang Juji made a pact with the masses: 'In this campaign, if we win no merit, do not drink wine!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; Huiyuan said, "When we left Fengtian, my commander Zhang Juji pledged to the men: 'In this campaign, whoever wins no merit shall not touch wine!

sentences.zh: 』臣不敢食其言。

translations.literal: ' I do not dare to go back on his words.
translations.idiomatic: ' I dare not break that vow.

sentences.zh: 」既行，有饋於道，惟惠元軍瓶罍不發。

translations.literal: " After they marched, there were gifts along the road, but only Huiyuan's army did not open its jars and goblets.
translations.idiomatic: " On the march, gifts of wine were offered along the road, yet only Huiyuan's men kept their flasks sealed.

sentences.zh: 帝咨嘆不已，璽書慰勞。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in admiration without cease and sent an imperial letter of consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled aloud and sent an imperial letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 俄以兵三千會諸將擊田悅，戰御河，奪三橋，惠元功多。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter with three thousand troops he joined the generals in attacking Tian Yue, fought at the Imperial River, seized three bridges, and Huiyuan's merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he led three thousand men to join the attack on Tian Yue, fought at the Imperial River, captured three bridges, and won the greatest share of credit.

sentences.zh: 以兵屬李懷光。

translations.literal: His troops were placed under Li Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: His command was placed under Li Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 及朱泚反，自河朔赴難，解奉天圍，加檢校工部尚書，攝貝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, from Hebei and Shuofang he rushed to relieve the crisis, lifted the siege of Fengtian, was promoted to Acting Minister of Works, and provisionally made prefect of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled he marched from the north to the emperor's aid, broke the siege of Fengtian, was made acting Minister of Works, and named provisional prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 詔惠元與神策行營節度使李晟、鄜坊節度使李建徽及懷光聯營便橋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Huiyuan, together with Li Sheng, military commissioner of the Shence field army, Li Jianhui, military commissioner of Fufang, and Huaiguang, to encamp jointly at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Huiyuan, Li Sheng of the Shence field army, Li Jianhui of Fufang, and Huaiguang to encamp together at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 晟知懷光且叛，移屯東渭橋。

translations.literal: Sheng knew Huaiguang was about to rebel and shifted his encampment to the Eastern Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, knowing Huaiguang was on the verge of rebellion, moved his camp to the Eastern Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士陸贄諫帝曰：「四將接壘，晟等兵寡位下，為懷光所易，勢不兩完。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi admonished the emperor, saying, "The four generals' camps adjoin one another; Sheng and the others have few troops and lower rank and are easily handled by Huaiguang—the situation cannot keep both sides intact.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi warned the emperor: "With all four camps adjacent, Sheng's force is small and his rank subordinate—Huaiguang can crush him at will. Both sides cannot survive this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 晟既慮變，請與惠元東徙，則建徽孤立。

translations.literal: Since Sheng already feared mutiny and requested to move east with Huiyuan, Jianhui would be left isolated.
translations.idiomatic: If Sheng, fearing treachery, asks to move east with Huiyuan, Jianhui will be left alone.

sentences.zh: 宜因晟行，合兩軍皆往，以備賊為解，趣裝進道，則懷光計無所施。

translations.literal: It is fitting to take advantage of Sheng's move and have both armies go together, using defense against the rebel as the explanation, urging equipment and advancing on the road—then Huaiguang's schemes would have nowhere to apply.
translations.idiomatic: Use Sheng's move as the occasion to send both armies east together, citing defense against the rebel as the reason; if they pack and march at once, Huaiguang's plot will fail.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，使神策將李升往伺。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow this advice and sent the Shence general Li Sheng to spy.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused and sent the Shence officer Li Sheng to investigate.

sentences.zh: 還奏：「懷光反明甚。

translations.literal: Returning, he reported, "Huaiguang's rebellion is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and reported, "Huaiguang's rebellion is unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 」是夕，奪二軍，惠元、建徽走奉天，懷光遣將冉宗馳騎追及於好畤。

translations.literal: " That evening he seized the two armies; Huiyuan and Jianhui fled to Fengtian; Huaiguang sent the general Ran Zong with galloping horsemen to overtake them at Haozhi.
translations.idiomatic: " That night he seized both armies. Huiyuan and Jianhui fled toward Fengtian; Huaiguang sent Ran Zong in pursuit and overtook them at Haozhi.

sentences.zh: 惠元被髮呼天，血流出眥，袒裼戰而死。

translations.literal: Huiyuan let his hair hang loose and cried to Heaven; blood flowed from the corners of his eyes; baring his torso he fought and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyuan tore loose his hair and cried to heaven, blood streaming from his eyes; stripped to the waist he fought until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 二子晟、暠匿井中，皆及害。

translations.literal: His two sons Sheng and Gao hid in a well and both met harm.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Sheng and Gao hid in a well and were both slain.

sentences.zh: 建徽獨免。

translations.literal: Jianhui alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jianhui escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔贈惠元尚書左僕射，晟殿中監，暠邠州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Huiyuan as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Sheng as Palace Supervisor, and Gao as prefect of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Huiyuan was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Sheng Palace Supervisor, and Gao prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 少子旻，字公素。

translations.literal: His youngest son Min, styled Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Min, courtesy name Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 惠元之死，被八創，墮別井，或救得免。

translations.literal: At Huiyuan's death he received eight wounds, fell into another well, and was perhaps rescued and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's death Min suffered eight wounds, fell into another well, and was pulled out alive.

sentences.zh: 歷邢州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盧從史既縛，潞軍潰，有驍卒五千，從史嘗以子視者，奔於旻，旻閉城不內。

translations.literal: When Lu Congshi was already bound, the Lu army collapsed; there were five thousand fierce soldiers whom Congshi had once regarded as sons—they fled to Min, and Min closed the city and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Congshi was captured the Lu army collapsed; five thousand elite troops whom Congshi had treated like sons fled to Min, and Min shut the gates against them.

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭曰：「奴失帥，今公有完城，又度支錢百萬在府，少賜之，為表天子求旌節。

translations.literal: The masses all wept and said, "We slaves have lost our commander; now you, my lord, have an intact city, and moreover a million strings of revenue funds are in the prefectural office—grant us a little and petition the Son of Heaven for a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and said, "We have lost our commander; you hold an intact city, and a million strings of revenue funds lie in the treasury—give us a share and petition the Son of Heaven for a commander's commission.

sentences.zh: 」旻開諭禍福遣之，眾感悟，遂還軍。

translations.literal: " Min opened the gates, explained fortune and misfortune, and sent them away; the masses were moved to understanding and thereupon returned to their army.
translations.idiomatic: " Min opened the gates, explained the consequences, and dismissed them; the men came to their senses and marched away.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉之，遷易州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong commended him and transferred him to be prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong praised him and transferred him to prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 王師討吳元濟，以唐州刺史提兵深入二百里，薄申州，拔外郛，殘其垣。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Wu Yuanji, as prefect of Tang Prefecture he led troops deep two hundred li, pressed close to Shen Prefecture, took the outer wall, and damaged its ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wu Yuanji, as prefect of Tang he led a deep thrust two hundred li, pressed Shen Prefecture, took its outer defenses, and battered its walls.

sentences.zh: 以功加御史中丞。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 容州西原蠻反，授本州經略招討使，擊定之。

translations.literal: When the Xiyuan barbarians of Rong Prefecture rebelled, he was appointed commissioner for pacification and suppression of that prefecture and struck to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiyuan tribes of Rong Prefecture rebelled, he was named commissioner for pacification and suppression and crushed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 進御史大夫，合邕、容兩管為一道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief, and the two circuits of Yong and Rong were combined into one command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and the Yong and Rong circuits were merged into a single command.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李元諒

translations.literal: Li Yuanliang
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanliang

sentences.zh: 李元諒，安息人。

translations.literal: Li Yuanliang was a man of Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanliang was of Parthian origin.

sentences.zh: 本安氏，少為宦官駱奉先養息，冒姓駱，名元光。

translations.literal: His original surname was An; in youth he was adopted and raised by the eunuch Luo Fengxian, took the surname Luo in pretense, and was named Yuanguang.
translations.idiomatic: Born of the An clan, he was raised in youth by the eunuch Luo Fengxian, took Luo as his surname, and was called Yuanguang.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，鷙敢有謀。

translations.literal: He had handsome beard and whiskers, was fierce, daring, and possessed stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome of beard, he was fierce, bold, and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 以宿衛積勞試太子詹事。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit in palace guard service he was tried as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For long service in the palace guard he was appointed provisional Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 李懷讓節度鎮國，署奏以自副。

translations.literal: When Li Huairang was military commissioner of Zhenguo, he appointed him in a memorial as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huairang commanded Zhenguo, he named Yuanliang his deputy in a memorial to court.

sentences.zh: 居軍十年，士心憚服。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the army ten years, and the soldiers hearts feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He remained with the army ten years, and the troops feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 德宗出奉天，賊遣將何望之襲華州，於是刺史董晉棄城走。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong went out to Fengtian, the rebels sent the general He Wangzhi to raid Hua Prefecture, whereupon the prefect Dong Jin abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong withdrew to Fengtian, the rebels sent He Wangzhi against Hua Prefecture; the prefect Dong Jin abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 望之欲聚兵以絕東道，元諒自潼關引兵徑薄其城，拔之。

translations.literal: Wangzhi wished to gather troops to cut off the eastern route; Yuanliang led troops from Tong Pass straight to press his city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi meant to mass troops and sever the eastern route; Yuanliang marched from Tong Pass, struck the city directly, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 時兵興倉卒，裹罽為鎧，剡蒿為矢，募兵數日至萬餘，軍氣乃振。

translations.literal: At the time arms were raised in haste; they wrapped felt as armor and carved artemisia as arrows; within several days recruited troops reached more than ten thousand, and army morale was restored.
translations.idiomatic: With war raised in haste, they wrapped felt for armor and carved artemisia for arrows; within days recruits topped ten thousand and the army's spirit revived.

sentences.zh: 賊來攻，輒卻。

translations.literal: When rebels came to attack, they were always repelled.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rebels attacked, they were driven back.

sentences.zh: 時尚可孤守藍田，元諒屯昭應，王權壁中渭橋，賊兵不能逾渭南。

translations.literal: At the time Shang Keji still held Lantian, Yuanliang encamped at Zhaoying, and Wang Quan fortified the Middle Wei Bridge; rebel troops could not cross south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Keji held Lantian, Yuanliang camped at Zhaoying, and Wang Quan walled the Middle Wei Bridge, so rebel forces could not cross south of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷鎮國軍節度使，封武康郡王。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and enfeoffed Prince of Wukang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made military commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and enfeoffed Prince of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔發豳、隴兵東討李希烈。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had dispatched Bin and Long troops east to campaign against Li Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had sent Bin and Long troops east against Li Xilie.

sentences.zh: 師方出關，泚使劉忠孝召還；

translations.literal: The army had just left the pass when Ci sent Liu Zhongxiao to summon them back;
translations.idiomatic: The column had barely cleared the pass when Ci sent Liu Zhongxiao to recall them;

sentences.zh: 至華陰，華陰尉李夷簡說驛官捕之，追及關，元諒斬以徇，所召兵不得入，由是華州獨完。

translations.literal: Reaching Huayin, the Huayin assistant Li Yijian persuaded the post station officials to seize him; pursued to the pass, Yuanliang beheaded him and displayed the head; the summoned troops could not enter, and thereby Hua Prefecture alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: At Huayin, assistant Li Yijian persuaded the courier station to arrest him; pursued to the pass, Yuanliang executed him as a warning, the recalled troops could not enter, and Hua Prefecture alone stayed intact.

sentences.zh: 俄詔元諒與李晟收京師，次浐西。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict ordered Yuanliang and Li Sheng to recover the capital; they halted west of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered Yuanliang and Li Sheng to retake the capital; they encamped west of Chan.

sentences.zh: 元諒先奮鏖賊，敗之，進屯苑東，晟使壞苑垣入。

translations.literal: Yuanliang first fought fiercely and routed the rebels, advanced to encamp east of the park, and Sheng had the park wall broken to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang led the fierce assault, routed the rebels, and encamped east of the imperial park while Sheng breached the park wall to enter.

sentences.zh: 泚連戰皆北，遂大潰，京師平。

translations.literal: Ci was defeated in successive battles and thereupon collapsed in great rout; the capital was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ci lost battle after battle, broke completely, and the capital was recovered.

sentences.zh: 讓功於晟，退壁近郊。

translations.literal: He yielded merit to Sheng and withdrew his camp to the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He ceded the credit to Sheng and withdrew his camp to the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書左僕射，實封戶五百，賜甲第、女樂、一子六品官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, granted five hundred substantive households, and given a mansion, female musicians, and one son an official of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Left Vice Director, granted five hundred substantive households, a mansion, female musicians, and a sixth-rank post for one son.

sentences.zh: 李懷光反，與馬燧、渾瑊討之。

translations.literal: When Li Huaiguang rebelled, he campaigned against him with Ma Sui and Hun Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiguang rebelled, he joined Ma Sui and Hun Jian against him.

sentences.zh: 其將徐廷光素易元諒，數嫚罵，為優胡戲，斥侮其祖。

translations.literal: His general Xu Tingguang had always looked down on Yuanliang, repeatedly insulted and reviled him, made him the butt of comic entertainers, and denounced and shamed his ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: His general Xu Tingguang had long despised Yuanliang, repeatedly abused him, mocked him in comic skits, and insulted his forebears.

sentences.zh: 又使約降，曰：「我降漢將耳。

translations.literal: He also sent men to negotiate surrender, saying, "I surrender only to a Han general.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent to negotiate surrender, saying, "I will yield only to a Han general.

sentences.zh: 」及馬燧至，降於燧。

translations.literal: " When Ma Sui arrived, he surrendered to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ma Sui arrived, he surrendered to Sui.

sentences.zh: 元諒見韓遊瑰曰：「彼詬吾祖，今日斬之，子助我乎？

translations.literal: Yuanliang saw Han Yougui and said, "He reviled my ancestors—today I shall behead him; will you help me?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang told Han Yougui, "He cursed my forebears—I mean to kill him today; will you aid me?

sentences.zh: 」許諾。

translations.literal: " He promised.
translations.idiomatic: " Yougui agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而遇諸道，即數其罪，叱左右斬之，詣燧謝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he encountered him among the various commands, immediately enumerated his crimes, shouted to the attendants to behead him, and went to Sui to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting him soon after among the allied commands, he listed his crimes, ordered his men to execute him, and went to apologize to Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧大怒，將殺元諒，遊瑰見曰：「殺一偏裨尚爾，即殺一節度，法宜如何？

translations.literal: Sui was greatly angered and was about to kill Yuanliang; Yougui appeared and said, "If killing a subordinate commander is treated thus, then killing a military commissioner—how should the law read?
translations.idiomatic: Sui was furious and would have killed Yuanliang; Yougui intervened: "You would kill a subordinate for this—what of killing a commissioner by law?

sentences.zh: 」燧默然。

translations.literal: " Sui was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Sui said nothing.

sentences.zh: 元諒請輸錢百萬勞軍自贖，瑊亦為請，燧赦之。

translations.literal: Yuanliang requested to pay a million strings to reward the army and redeem himself; Jian also pleaded for him, and Sui pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang offered a million strings to reward the troops in ransom; Jian pleaded too, and Sui pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 帝以專殺，恐有司劾治，前詔勿論。

translations.literal: Because of unauthorized killing, the emperor feared the authorities would impeach and punish him, and issued a prior edict that it should not be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing prosecution for summary execution, the emperor issued a prior edict that the matter should not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，吐蕃請盟，詔以軍從瑊會平涼，元諒軍潘原、遊瑰軍洛口以為援。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan the Tibetans requested alliance; an edict ordered troops to follow Jian to meet at Pingliang, with Yuanliang's army at Panyuan and Yougui's at Luokou as support.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year three the Tibetans sought alliance; troops were ordered to follow Jian to Pingliang, Yuanliang at Panyuan and Yougui at Luokou as reserve.

sentences.zh: 元諒曰：「潘原去平涼七十里，虜詐不情，如有急，何以赴？

translations.literal: Yuanliang said, "Panyuan is seventy li from Pingliang; the barbarians are deceitful and insincere—if there is urgency, how can we respond?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang said, "Panyuan lies seventy li from Pingliang; the enemy is treacherous—if trouble comes, how can we aid you?

sentences.zh: 請與公連屯。

translations.literal: Please encamp together with you.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to camp jointly with you.

sentences.zh: 」瑊以違詔，不聽。

translations.literal: " Jian, citing violation of the edict, did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian refused, citing the edict.

sentences.zh: 瑊壁盟所二十里，元諒密徙營次之。

translations.literal: Jian fortified twenty li from the alliance site; Yuanliang secretly moved his camp next to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian encamped twenty li from the treaty ground; Yuanliang quietly shifted camp beside him.

sentences.zh: 既會，元諒望雲物曰：「不詳，虜必有變！

translations.literal: When they met, Yuanliang looked at the clouds and said, "Inauspicious—the barbarians must have a change!
translations.idiomatic: At the meeting Yuanliang studied the sky and said, "Ill omens—the barbarians will strike!

sentences.zh: 」傳令約部伍出陣。

translations.literal: " He transmitted orders for the units to form battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered his ranks to deploy.

sentences.zh: 俄而虜劫盟，瑊奔還，元諒兵成列出，而涇原節度使李觀亦以精兵五千伏險，與元諒相表裏，虜騎乃解。

translations.literal: Shortly the barbarians raided the alliance; Jian fled back; Yuanliang's troops deployed in full array, and the Jingyuan military commissioner Li Guan also lay five thousand elite troops in ambush in difficult terrain, coordinating inside and outside with Yuanliang, and the barbarian cavalry thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tibetans broke the treaty; Jian fled; Yuanliang's men stood in full array; Li Guan of Jingyuan also hid five thousand elite troops in rough ground to coordinate with him, and the enemy cavalry withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元諒遣車重先，而與瑊振旅徐還，時以為有古良將風。

translations.literal: Yuanliang sent the baggage train ahead and with Jian slowly withdrew the army in good order; at the time he was thought to have the manner of ancient worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang sent the baggage ahead and withdrew in good order with Jian—men said he had the bearing of the old masters of war.

sentences.zh: 是會也，微元諒、觀二人，瑊且不免。

translations.literal: At this meeting, but for Yuanliang and Guan the two men, Jian would scarcely have escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At that parley, but for Yuanliang and Guan, Jian would hardly have survived.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉嘆，賜善馬金幣良厚，因賜姓及名。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in admiration and granted excellent horses and gold and coins in great abundance, and thereby bestowed surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and rewarded him richly with fine horses, gold, and coin, and bestowed surname and personal name.

sentences.zh: 更節度隴右，治良原。

translations.literal: He was again made military commissioner of Longyou and administered Liangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to command Longyou from Liangyuan.

sentences.zh: 良原隍堞湮圮，旁皆平林薦草，虜入寇，常牧馬休徒於此。

translations.literal: The moats and ramparts of Liangyuan were buried and ruined; on all sides were level woods and rank grass; when barbarians entered to raid, they often pastured horses and rested troops here.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyuan's walls were collapsed; level woods and tall grass surrounded it; raiders often pastured and camped there.

sentences.zh: 元諒培高浚淵，身執苦與士卒均，菑翳榛莽，辟美田數十里，勸士墾藝，歲入粟菽數十萬斛，什具畢給。

translations.literal: Yuanliang raised the heights and deepened the moats, personally took up hardship equal to the soldiers, cleared overgrown brambles, opened fine fields for several tens of li, urged the men to reclaim and plant, and yearly income of grain and beans reached several hundred thousand hu; all equipment was fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He raised ramparts and deepened moats, shared the soldiers' labor, cleared scrub for fields across tens of li, urged cultivation, and harvested hundreds of thousands of hu yearly with full equipment.

sentences.zh: 又築連弩臺，遠烽偵，為守備，進據勢勝，列新壁。

translations.literal: He also built repeating-crossbow towers, distant beacon watch, made defensive preparations, advanced to hold advantageous ground, and arrayed new walls.
translations.idiomatic: He built repeating-crossbow towers and distant beacons, strengthened defenses, seized commanding ground, and laid new walls.

sentences.zh: 虜至無所掠，戰又輒北，由是涇、隴以安，西戎憚之。

translations.literal: When barbarians came there was nothing to plunder; in battle they were repeatedly driven north; thereby Jing and Long were secured and the western Rong feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders found nothing to seize and were repeatedly beaten back; Jing and Long grew secure and the western tribes feared him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈司空，謚曰莊威。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two, was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works, and given the posthumous title Zhuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two, was posthumously made Minister of Works, and given the posthumous title Zhuangwei.

sentences.zh: 李觀，其先自趙郡徙洛陽，故為洛陽人。

translations.literal: Li Guan—his forebears had moved from Zhao Commandery to Luoyang, and so he was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guan's ancestors had moved from Zhao Commandery to Luoyang; he was counted a Luoyang man.

sentences.zh: 少沈厚寡言。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep, steady, and sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was grave, steady, and sparing of speech.

sentences.zh: 以策干朔方節度使郭子儀，子儀遣佐坊州刺史吳伷為防遏使。

translations.literal: With a policy memorandum he approached the Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi; Ziyi sent him to assist the Fangzhou prefect Wu Xian as defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a policy plan to Guo Ziyi, who sent him to assist Fangzhou prefect Wu Xian as defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以親喪解。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃內寇，代宗幸陜，觀隱盩厔，率鄉里子姓千人守黑水，虜不敢侵。

translations.literal: When Tibetans raided within the borders, Emperor Daizong went to Shan; Guan hid at Zhouzhi, led a thousand men of his district and clan to guard Heishui, and the barbarians did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided inland, Daizong withdrew to Shan; Guan lay hidden at Zhouzhi and led a thousand kinsmen to hold Heishui, and the enemy did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使楊慎微奏為偏將，徐浩、李勉代節度，常倚以軍政，數捕平劇賊。

translations.literal: The Lingnan military commissioner Yang Shenwei memorialized him as a subordinate general; Xu Hao and Li Mian succeeded as commissioners and constantly relied on him for military affairs, repeatedly capturing and pacifying fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenwei of Lingnan recommended him as a subordinate general; Xu Hao and Li Mian, succeeding as commissioners, relied on him in military affairs and repeatedly crushed major bandits.

sentences.zh: 遷大將，試殿中監，召為右龍武將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to great general, tried as Palace Supervisor, and summoned as Right Dragon Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to great general, served provisionally as Palace Supervisor, and was summoned as Right Dragon Martial General.

sentences.zh: 涇師叛，觀適番上，即領兵千餘扈德宗奉天。

translations.literal: When the Jing troops rebelled, Guan happened to be on palace rotation duty and immediately led more than a thousand troops to escort Emperor Dezong to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing army mutinied, Guan was on palace duty and at once led over a thousand men to escort Dezong to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 詔盡察諸軍，整飭誰邏，增募五千人，鼙旝歡豎，士氣益振。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to inspect all armies, put in order who would return, recruited five thousand more men, drums and banners were joyfully raised, and morale grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he inspected all armies, organized the return march, recruited five thousand more, and morale surged as drums and banners were raised.

sentences.zh: 賜封戶二百，授二子八品官。

translations.literal: He was granted two hundred fief households and two sons officials of the eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He received two hundred fief households and eighth-rank posts for two sons.

sentences.zh: 從至梁州。

translations.literal: He followed to Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝還，詔總後軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, an edict ordered him to command the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return, an edict placed him in command of the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 擢四鎮、北庭行軍涇原節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of Jingyuan in the Four Garrisons and Northern Court field army.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to Jingyuan commissioner in the Four Garrisons and Northern Court field command.

sentences.zh: 在屯四年，訓部伍，儲藏饒衍。

translations.literal: In camp four years he trained the ranks and stores overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Four years in camp he drilled the ranks and filled the granaries.

sentences.zh: 平涼之盟，吐蕃不得志。

translations.literal: At the Pingliang alliance the Tibetans did not achieve their aim.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang the Tibetans failed to gain their ends.

sentences.zh: 是年，觀入朝，前一日就道，虜至期出精騎狙擊，不及，去。

translations.literal: That year Guan entered court; the day before he set out on the road, barbarians came on schedule with elite cavalry to ambush and strike but could not catch him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guan went to court; the day before he left, Tibetans timed elite cavalry to ambush him but missed him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以少府監檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was made Acting Minister of Works while serving as Director of the Palace Armory.
translations.idiomatic: He was named acting Minister of Works while retaining the Directorship of the Palace Armory.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰

translations.literal: Han Yougui
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰，靈州靈武人，始為郭子儀裨將。

translations.literal: Han Yougui was a man of Lingwu in Ling Prefecture and at first was a lieutenant general under Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui of Lingwu in Ling Prefecture began as a lieutenant under Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，使阿史那從禮將同羅、突厥五千騎偽降於朔方，出塞門，誘河曲九蕃府、六胡叛，部落凡五十萬。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Ashina Congli with five thousand Tongluo and Turkic horsemen to feign surrender to Shuofang, go out beyond the frontier pass, entice the Nine Fan Offices and Six Hu of the river bend to rebel—the tribes altogether five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Ashina Congli with five thousand Tongluo and Turk horsemen in false surrender to Shuofang, lured the Nine Fan Offices and Six Hu of the river bend to revolt—five hundred thousand tribesmen in all.

sentences.zh: 子儀使遊瑰率辛京杲擊破之，九蕃府還附。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent Yougui leading Xin Jinggao to defeat them, and the Nine Fan Offices returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent Yougui with Xin Jinggao to rout them, and the Nine Fan Offices returned to the fold.

sentences.zh: 累進邠寧節度留後。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to acting military commissioner of Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to acting commissioner of Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 奉天之狩，兵未集，遊瑰與慶州刺史論惟明以兵三千來赴，自乾陵北趨醴泉，未至，有詔引軍屯便橋。

translations.literal: During the hunt at Fengtian the armies were not yet gathered; Yougui and the Qingzhou prefect Lun Weiming came with three thousand troops, hastened north of Qianling toward Liquan; before they arrived, an edict recalled the army to encamp at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At Dezong's withdrawal to Fengtian, before armies had massed, Yougui and Qingzhou prefect Lun Weiming brought three thousand men north of Qianling toward Liquan; before they arrived, an edict ordered them to Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 次泥泉，與泚兵值，遊瑰欲還奉天，監軍翟文秀曰：「吾壁於此，賊敢逾我而西，可夾攻取之。

translations.literal: Halting at Niquan, they met Ci's troops; Yougui wished to return to Fengtian; the army supervisor Zhai Wenxiu said, "We fortify here; if rebels dare pass west of us, we can take them in a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: At Niquan they met Zhu Ci's force; Yougui wanted to return to Fengtian; supervisor Zhai Wenxiu said, "If we hold here, rebels cannot pass west of us without being caught between two fires.

sentences.zh: 今入奉天，賊亦隨至，是引賊迫天子也。

translations.literal: If we now enter Fengtian, the rebels will also follow, and that is leading rebels to press the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Enter Fengtian now and the rebels follow—that drives the enemy upon the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」遊瑰曰：「不然，我寡賊眾。

translations.literal: " Yougui said, "Not so—we are few and the rebels many.
translations.idiomatic: " Yougui said, "No—we are few, they many.

sentences.zh: 彼分以亢我，餘眾猶能鼓而西也，不如先入衛天子。

translations.literal: If they divide to oppose us, the remainder can still drum westward; better first enter to guard the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If they divide to hold us, the rest can still march west; better to reach the emperor first.

sentences.zh: 且奉天無強卒，安得夾攻？

translations.literal: Moreover Fengtian has no strong troops—how can there be a pincer?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Fengtian has no strong garrison—what pincer?

sentences.zh: 吾士乏且寒，賊以利誘之，眾且潰。

translations.literal: Our men are weary and cold; the rebels will entice them with profit and the masses will collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Our men are weary and cold; the enemy will bribe them and the ranks will break.

sentences.zh: 」遂還奉天。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they returned to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: " They turned back to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 泚兵躡攻之，戰不利；

translations.literal: Ci's troops pursued and attacked; the battle went badly;
translations.idiomatic: Ci's men pursued; the fight went ill;

sentences.zh: 泚兵奪門，遊瑰殊死戰，乃解。

translations.literal: Ci's troops seized the gate; Yougui fought desperately to the death and only then was the crisis resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Ci's troops seized the gate; Yougui fought desperately until the danger passed.

sentences.zh: 泚大治戰棚、雲橋，士皆懼，遊瑰曰：「賊取佛祠幹木為攻具，可以火之。

translations.literal: Ci greatly prepared battle sheds and cloud bridges; the soldiers were all afraid; Yougui said, "The rebels take dry timber from Buddhist shrines as siege engines—we can burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Ci built great siege sheds and cloud bridges; the men were terrified; Yougui said, "They take dry timber from temples for engines—we can burn them.

sentences.zh: 」既而賊大噪攻南雉，遊瑰曰：「是分吾力也。

translations.literal: " Shortly the rebels made a great clamor attacking the southern bastion; Yougui said, "This divides our strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the rebels stormed the southern bastion; Yougui said, "That splits our force.

sentences.zh: 」趨北雉，遣將郭詢、郭廷玉以銳士三百傅滿直出，火其棚，投薪於中，風返，棚皆燼，賊氣沮。

translations.literal: " He hurried to the northern bastion and sent the generals Guo Xun and Guo Tingyu with three hundred elite troops carrying full fuel to rush straight out, set fire to the sheds, and cast fuel within; the wind turned back and the sheds were all ash; rebel morale was crushed.
translations.idiomatic: " He raced to the north bastion and sent Guo Xun and Guo Tingyu with three hundred picked men to fire the sheds; the wind blew back, the works burned, and rebel spirit broke.

sentences.zh: 故諸將推遊瑰赴難功第一。

translations.literal: Therefore the various generals ranked Yougui first in merit for rushing to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders therefore ranked Yougui first in merit for the relief of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 帝以衛軍無職局，軍置統軍一員，以遊瑰、惟明、賈隱林處之。

translations.literal: Because the guard army had no formal offices, one post of army commander was established for Yougui, Weiming, and Jia Yinlin.
translations.idiomatic: Because the guard army lacked formal posts, one army commander was created for Yougui, Weiming, and Jia Yinlin.

sentences.zh: 李懷光叛，誘遊瑰為變，遊瑰白髮其書。

translations.literal: When Li Huaiguang rebelled he enticed Yougui to mutiny; Yougui reported and displayed his letter.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiguang rebelled he tried to win Yougui; Yougui exposed his letter to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿可謂忠義矣！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You may be called loyal and righteous!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are truly loyal!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣安知忠義？

translations.literal: " He answered, "How should your servant know loyalty and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "How should I know loyalty?

sentences.zh: 但懷光誤臣，使震驚乘輿，後持臣自解。

translations.literal: Only Huaiguang misled your servant, making me alarm the imperial carriage; afterward he would hold your servant to excuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang tricked me into alarming the imperial carriage, then meant to use me as his excuse.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其誠，從問：「計欲安出？

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his sincerity and followed by asking, "What plan should emerge?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor admired his candor and asked, "What is your plan?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「懷光總諸府兵，怙以為亂。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Huaiguang commands the troops of the various prefectures and relies on them to make disorder.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "Huaiguang commands troops from many prefectures and trusts them for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今邠有張昕，靈武有寧薍景璿，河中有呂鳴嶽，振武有杜從政，潼關有李朝臣，渭北有竇覦，皆守將也。

translations.literal: Now at Bin there is Zhang Xin, at Lingwu Ning Yin Jingxuan, at Hezhong Lü Mingyue, at Zhenwu Du Congzheng, at Tong Pass Li Zhaochen, north of the Wei Dou Kan—all garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Bin has Zhang Xin, Lingwu Ning Yin Jingxuan, Hezhong Lü Mingyue, Zhenwu Du Congzheng, Tong Pass Li Zhaochen, north of the Wei Dou Kan—all loyal garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 陛下以其眾與地授之，罷懷光權，而尊以元功，諸將仰首，各聽其帥，彼安能以亂？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, granting them his masses and territory, removes Huaiguang's power while honoring him with the rank of supreme merit; the generals will look up and each obey his own commander—how can he make disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Give them his troops and territory, strip Huaiguang of power, honor him with empty rank, and each commander will obey his own leader—how then can he rebel?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「罷懷光權而泚益張，若何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "If we remove Huaiguang's power, Ci will grow stronger—what then?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Remove Huaiguang and Ci grows stronger—what then?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下約士以不次之賞，今貢賦方至，發而酬之，其守自固。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Your Majesty has promised the troops extraordinary rewards; now tribute is arriving—issue it in payment and their defense will hold of itself.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "You promised extraordinary rewards; tribute is arriving—pay them from it and the garrisons will hold.

sentences.zh: 邠有萬精甲，臣得將之，可以誅賊。

translations.literal: At Bin there are ten thousand elite armored troops; if your servant may command them, the rebels can be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin has ten thousand elite armored men; give me command of them and the rebels can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 四方杖義而起，賊不足慮。

translations.literal: Loyalty to righteousness rises on all sides—the rebels are not worth anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous armies are rising everywhere—the rebels are no great worry.

sentences.zh: 」帝美其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended the plan.

sentences.zh: 會懷光誘復至，渾瑊得書，稍嚴卒以警。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang's enticements came again, Hun Jian received a letter and somewhat tightened the troops as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang tried again to win him over; Hun Jian received his letter and tightened discipline among the troops.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰不知，發怒，嫚罵瑊。

translations.literal: Yougui did not know and grew angry, insulting and reviling Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui knew nothing of it and flew into a rage, abusing Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝疑有變，即日幸梁州，遊瑰使子從帝。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected a change and that very day went to Liang Prefecture; Yougui sent his son to follow the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting treachery, the emperor withdrew to Liangzhou that day; Yougui sent his son to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 懷光檄假遊瑰邠州刺史，欲因張昕殺之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang issued a proclamation in Yougui's name as prefect of Bin, wishing to use Zhang Xin to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang forged a commission making Yougui prefect of Bin, intending Zhang Xin to kill him.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰既失兵，不知所圖。

translations.literal: Yougui had already lost his army and did not know what plan to make.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his command, Yougui was at a loss.

sentences.zh: 有客劉南金說曰：「邠有留甲，可以立功，殆天假也！

translations.literal: A guest, Liu Nanjin, advised, saying, "At Bin there are troops left behind—merit can be won; perhaps Heaven lends the chance!
translations.idiomatic: A retainer, Liu Nanjin, said, "Bin still holds a garrison—you can win glory; perhaps Heaven lends the chance!

sentences.zh: 」遊瑰悟，誘舊部兵八百馳入邠，說昕曰：「懷光自蹈禍機，公今可取富貴，無共汙不義也。

translations.literal: " Yougui understood, enticed eight hundred of his old troops to gallop into Bin, and said to Xin, "Huaiguang has plunged himself into disaster—you can now seize wealth and honor; do not share in unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: " Yougui took the hint, rallied eight hundred old soldiers into Bin, and told Xin, "Huaiguang has courted ruin—you can seize fortune now; do not share his crime.

sentences.zh: 我願以麾下為公先驅。

translations.literal: I wish to take those under my command as your vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Let my men lead your attack.

sentences.zh: 」昕不聽。

translations.literal: " Xin would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin refused.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰移疾不出，陰結其將高固等。

translations.literal: Yougui feigned illness and did not go out, secretly joining his generals Gao Gu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui pretended illness and stayed within, secretly winning Gao Gu and other officers.

sentences.zh: 昕欲殺遊瑰，戒左右衷甲入。

translations.literal: Xin wished to kill Yougui and warned the attendants to wear armor beneath their robes when entering.
translations.idiomatic: Xin plotted to kill Yougui and ordered his men to enter wearing hidden armor.

sentences.zh: 昕小史李岌潛白遊瑰，伏甲先起，高固等應之，斬昕首以聞。

translations.literal: Xin's junior clerk Li Ji secretly informed Yougui; hidden armor rose first, Gao Gu and others responded, and they beheaded Xin and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's clerk Li Ji warned Yougui; Yougui's hidden troops struck first, Gao Gu joined in, and they beheaded Xin and reported to court.

sentences.zh: 時懷光子玫在邠，遊瑰衛出之，曰：「殺之只以怒敵，至必遽，不如舍之。

translations.literal: At the time Huaiguang's son Mei was at Bin; Yougui guarded and escorted him out, saying, "Killing him would only anger the enemy; when he arrives he will flee at once—better to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's son Mei was at Bin; Yougui escorted him out, saying, "Kill him and you only enrage the enemy; he will flee at once—better spare him.

sentences.zh: 」玫至涇陽，懷光遂走蒲州。

translations.literal: " When Mei reached Jingyang, Huaiguang thereupon fled to Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Mei reached Jingyang and Huaiguang fled to Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰屯七盤，受李晟節度。

translations.literal: Yougui encamped at Qipan and accepted Li Sheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui encamped at Qipan under Li Sheng's command.

sentences.zh: 詔拜邠寧節度使，遂會渾瑊於奉天，與瑊、戴休顏分扼京西要險。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military commissioner of Bin-Ning; he thereupon joined Hun Jian at Fengtian and with Jian and Dai Xiuyan divided control of the vital passes west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he became commissioner of Bin-Ning, joined Hun Jian at Fengtian, and with Jian and Dai Xiuyan held the key passes west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 李晟入長安，遊瑰破泚兵咸陽。

translations.literal: When Li Sheng entered Chang'an, Yougui defeated Ci's troops at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng entered Chang'an, Yougui routed Zhu Ci's men at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 泚走涇州，遊瑰使諭涇將楊澄，澄拒不納，泚遂敗。

translations.literal: Ci fled to Jing Prefecture; Yougui sent men to persuade the Jing general Yang Cheng; Cheng refused and would not accept him, and Ci thereupon was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ci fled to Jingzhou; Yougui urged Jing general Yang Cheng to turn on him; Cheng refused, and Ci was undone.

sentences.zh: 京師平，遷檢校尚書左僕射，實封戶四百。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted four hundred substantive households.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered he was made acting Left Vice Director and granted four hundred substantive households.

sentences.zh: 帝至自興元，遊瑰及瑊、休顏從，而李晟、尚可孤、李元諒奉迎，論功與瑊等皆第一。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived from Xingyuan, Yougui followed with Jian and Xiuyan, while Li Sheng, Shang Keji, and Li Yuanliang came to welcome him; in discussing merit, with Jian and the others he ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Xingyuan, Yougui marched with Jian and Xiuyan while Li Sheng, Shang Keji, and Li Yuanliang met him; in the reckoning of merit he ranked with Jian at the top.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰還屯邠寧。

translations.literal: Yougui returned to garrison Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui returned to garrison Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 懷光寇同州，瑊、元諒敗於乾坑。

translations.literal: Huaiguang raided Tong Prefecture; Jian and Yuanliang were defeated at Qiankeng.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang struck Tong Prefecture; Jian and Yuanliang were beaten at Qiankeng.

sentences.zh: 詔遊瑰率兵並力，敗賊眾五千於屯。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yougui to lead troops in combined strength and defeat five thousand of the rebel masses at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yougui to join the assault and destroy five thousand rebels at the camp.

sentences.zh: 遂會瑊、馬燧圍蒲城。

translations.literal: He thereupon joined Jian and Ma Sui in besieging Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Jian and Ma Sui in the siege of Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 師次焦籬堡，守將尉珪降。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jiaoli Fort; the defending general Wei Gui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jiaoli Fort; defender Wei Gui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 懷光見勢單蹙，乃縊死。

translations.literal: Huaiguang saw his position isolated and pressed and thereupon hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing himself cornered, Huaiguang hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，吐蕃入涇、隴、邠、寧，遊瑰追至安化，虜營合水北。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan the Tibetans entered Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning; Yougui pursued to Anhua; the barbarian camp was north of the He River at Heshui.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year two Tibetans raided Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning; Yougui pursued to Anhua where the enemy camped north of Heshui.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰策曰：「賊行無人地，必怠，可襲取之。

translations.literal: Yougui strategized, saying, "The rebels march through uninhabited land and must grow slack—we can strike and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui said, "They march through empty country and will grow careless—we can strike them.

sentences.zh: 」使將史履澄夜領兵五百入其營，斬數百級，取馬五千。

translations.literal: " He sent the general Shi Lvcheng by night to lead five hundred troops into their camp, beheaded several hundred, and took five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Shi Lvcheng with five hundred men by night into their camp, killed hundreds, and seized five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 遲明，虜以兵尾擊，遊瑰羅幟自衛，鼙鼓四發，虜驚潰去。

translations.literal: At dawn the barbarians struck from the rear; Yougui arrayed banners to shield himself, drums and gongs sounded on four sides, and the barbarians fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy pursued; Yougui drew up banners, beat drums on every side, and the Tibetans broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復圍鹽州，刺史杜彥光約與之城，吐蕃許之，又取銀、夏、麟等州。

translations.literal: That year they again besieged Salt Prefecture; the prefect Du Yanguang agreed to hand over the city; the Tibetans promised this and also took Yin, Xia, Lin, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That year they besieged Salt Prefecture again; prefect Du Yanguang agreed to surrender; the Tibetans promised peace and seized Yin, Xia, Lin, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰請收鹽州以斷戎人走集：「虜入漢，食禾菽，方春而病，此天亡時也。

translations.literal: Yougui requested to recover Salt Prefecture to cut off the Rong people's routes of assembly: "When barbarians enter Han territory they eat grain and beans; at spring they fall ill—this is the time Heaven destroys them.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui urged retaking Salt Prefecture to sever Tibetan lines of movement: "When they enter Han lands they eat grain; in spring they sicken—Heaven's moment to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 」有詔李元諒、韓全義率師一萬，會遊瑰收鹽州。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Li Yuanliang and Han Quanyi to lead ten thousand troops and join Yougui in recovering Salt Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Li Yuanliang and Han Quanyi with ten thousand men to join Yougui in retaking Salt.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃請修清水盟，以歸侵地，馬燧為之請。

translations.literal: The Tibetans requested to renew the Qingshui treaty and return the invaded lands; Ma Sui pleaded for them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans asked to renew the Qingshui treaty and return seized lands; Ma Sui supported them.

sentences.zh: 詔問遊瑰，答曰：「西戎弱則請盟，強則入寇。

translations.literal: An edict asked Yougui; he answered, "When the western Rong are weak they request alliance; when strong they enter to raid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Yougui, who replied, "When weak the western tribes sue for peace; when strong they raid.

sentences.zh: 今侵地益深而乞盟，詐我也！

translations.literal: Now they invade deeper yet beg alliance—it is deceit!
translations.idiomatic: They deepen their invasion yet beg peace—that is deceit!

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 會盟平涼，詔遊瑰以軍屯洛口。

translations.literal: When the alliance met at Pingliang, an edict ordered Yougui to encamp his army at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: For the Pingliang treaty the emperor ordered Yougui to camp at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 盟之日，遊瑰以勁騎五百待非常，令曰：「即有變，急趨柏泉以分虜勢。

translations.literal: On the day of alliance Yougui kept five hundred crack horsemen ready for the unexpected and ordered, "If there is a change, hurry to Baiquan to divide the barbarian force.
translations.idiomatic: On treaty day Yougui held five hundred elite horsemen in reserve with orders: "If anything goes wrong, rush to Baiquan to split the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」瑊被劫，馳以免，虜見兵出，即解去。

translations.literal: " Jian was seized in the raid and galloped to escape; the barbarians saw troops emerge and thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian was ambushed but escaped; the enemy saw troops deploy and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後吐蕃寇大回原，遊瑰方壁長武，即選騎八百迎擊，自引兵繼之。

translations.literal: Later the Tibetans raided Dayuan Plain; Yougui was fortifying Changwu and at once selected eight hundred horsemen to meet the attack, himself leading troops after.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tibetans raided Dayuan Plain while Yougui was at Changwu; he sent eight hundred horsemen to meet them and followed with the main body.

sentences.zh: 監軍以為戎不可易，答曰：「賊攻豐義，今遊騎先破，則彼大眾不敢前，豐義全矣！

translations.literal: The army supervisor thought the Rong could not be lightly challenged; he answered, "The rebels attack Fengyi; if our roaming cavalry breaks them first, their great mass will not dare advance and Fengyi will be saved!
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor said the enemy could not be provoked; Yougui replied, "They strike Fengyi—if our vanguard breaks them first, their main force will not advance and Fengyi is saved!

sentences.zh: 」戰南原，敗之，吐蕃夜遁。

translations.literal: " Fighting on the southern plain, he defeated them and the Tibetans fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: " He fought on the southern plain, routed them, and the Tibetans fled by night.

sentences.zh: 會子欽緒以射生將衛京師，與妖人李廣弘謀反，謀泄，奔邠州，中人捕斬，以狀示遊瑰。

translations.literal: When his son Qinxu came as a bow-shot officer to guard the capital and plotted rebellion with the sorcerer Li Guanghong, the plot leaked; he fled to Bin Prefecture and the palace agents captured and beheaded him, showing the report to Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinxu, a bow-shot officer guarding the capital, plotted with sorcerer Li Guanghong; exposed, he fled to Bin and was executed; the report was shown to Yougui.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰懼，求歸死京師，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yougui was afraid and requested to return and die in the capital; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui feared punishment and asked to return to face death in the capital; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又執欽緒二息送京師，帝亦原之。

translations.literal: He also seized Qinxu's two sons and sent them to the capital; the emperor also pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qinxu's two young sons to the capital; the emperor pardoned them as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入朝，素服聽命，有詔復位，勞遇如故。

translations.literal: Before long he entered court in plain dress to await orders; an edict restored his post and he was received with favor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he came to court in plain dress to submit; an edict restored him and he was received as before.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰盛言城豐義以遏虜侵。

translations.literal: Yougui strongly urged fortifying Fengyi to check barbarian invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui urged building up Fengyi to block barbarian raids.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，趣還軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and urged him to return to the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and ordered him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 初，遊瑰之朝，眾謂且得罪，故賫送殊薄。

translations.literal: At first, when Yougui went to court, the masses said he would surely be punished, and so his gifts for presentation were very meager.
translations.idiomatic: When he first went to court men expected disgrace, so his gifts to the emperor were meager.

sentences.zh: 既還，舉軍不自安。

translations.literal: After he returned, the whole army was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the entire army was uneasy.

sentences.zh: 大將范希朝善兵，遊瑰畏其逼，欲誅之，希朝奔鳳翔，帝聞，召入宿衛。

translations.literal: The great general Fan Xichao was skilled in warfare; Yougui feared his pressure and wished to execute him; Xichao fled to Fengxiang and, when the emperor heard, summoned him into palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Great general Fan Xichao was a master of war; Yougui feared him and plotted his death; Xichao fled to Fengxiang and was summoned into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰遣兵築豐義，才二板而潰，寧卒數百大掠，遊瑰不能禁。

translations.literal: Yougui sent troops to build Fengyi; after only two courses of wall it collapsed; several hundred Ning troops plundered on a great scale and Yougui could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui sent men to build Fengyi; after two courses the work collapsed; hundreds of Ning soldiers looted wildly and he could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 詔用張獻甫代之。

translations.literal: An edict employed Zhang Xianfu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replaced him with Zhang Xianfu.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰畏亂，委軍輕出，還京師，拜右龍武統軍。

translations.literal: Yougui feared disorder, entrusted the army and left lightly, returned to the capital, and was appointed commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing mutiny, he left the army lightly and returned to court as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 廣弘者，自言宗室子。

translations.literal: Guanghong—he claimed to be a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghong claimed descent from the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 始為浮屠，妄曰：「我嘗見嶽、瀆神，當作天子，可復冠。

translations.literal: At first he was a Buddhist monk and falsely said, "I once saw the gods of the sacred mountains and rivers—I am to become Son of Heaven and may again wear the cap.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a Buddhist monk and declared he had seen the river and mountain gods and was destined to be emperor and could wear the crown again.

sentences.zh: 」男子董昌舍廣弘於資敬寺，召相工唐郛視之，教郛告人曰：「廣弘且大貴。

translations.literal: " The man Dong Chang lodged Guanghong at Zijing Temple, summoned the physiognomist Tang Fu to examine him, and taught Fu to tell people, "Guanghong is about to reach great honor.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Chang housed him at Zijing Temple and had physiognomist Tang Fu proclaim that Guanghong would soon rise to greatness.

sentences.zh: 」乃誘欽緒、神策將魏循、李傪、越州參軍事劉昉等作亂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he enticed Qinxu, the Shence general Wei Xun, Li Song, and the Yuezhou staff member Liu Fang and others to make disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew in Qinxu, Shence generals Wei Xun and Li Song, and Yuezhou staff officer Liu Fang to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 昉家數具酒大會廣弘所，陰相署置。

translations.literal: Fang's household repeatedly set out wine for great gatherings at Guanghong's place, secretly conferring appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang's house held repeated feasts at Guanghong's lodging where ranks were secretly assigned.

sentences.zh: 又妄曰：「神戒我十月十日趣舉。

translations.literal: He also falsely said, "The spirits warn me to rise on the tenth day of the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared the spirits commanded an uprising on the tenth day of the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 」約欽緒夜擊鼓，噪淩霄門，焚飛龍廄，循等以神策兵迎廣弘，事捷，大剽三日。

translations.literal: " They agreed that Qinxu would strike the drum by night, clamor at Lingxiao Gate, burn the Flying Dragon stable, and Xun and others with Shence troops would welcome Guanghong; when the affair succeeded, they would plunder greatly for three days.
translations.idiomatic: They planned for Qinxu to beat drums at night, storm Lingxiao Gate, burn the Flying Dragon stable, and Xun's Shence troops would install Guanghong, then loot for three days.
